title: MolmoSpaces-CommonSense: Evaluating Commonsense in Robotic Manipulation Policies; submitted: 2026-10-30; categories: cs.RO; authors: Arjun Guru; Max Argus; Jae Sung Park; Jiafei Duan; Ali Farhadi; Ranjay Krishna; abstract: Real-world robotic manipulation requires reasoning about cluttered scenes, partially observable or hidden objects, and semantically appropriate actions, in addition to low-level execution within those scenes. However, existing simulation benchmarks primarily test the latter and remain dominated by comparatively clean environments with limited clutter and narrowly scoped task structure, leaving many forms of commonsense reasoning untested. We address this by introducing a taxonomy of reasoning processes for robotic manipulation grounded in developmental cognitive science. We operationalize this taxonomy through a new benchmark of robot tasks, MolmoSpaces-CommonSense, that requires reasoning about occlusion, containment, support relations, semantically correct grasp points, spatial affordances, and hidden objects.
